findings.title: Semantic NLP Failure: 'comfortable sneakers under 100' Returns Irrelevant Results
findings.impact_stat: Footwear ecommerce conversion rate sits at ~2.2% — among the lowest in fashion ecommerce due to sizing complexity
findings.actual_behavior: Results returned (185KB page) but custom /zgw gateway cannot parse multi-attribute NL queries — price qualifier and comfort attribute ignored
findings.algolia_solution: NeuralSearch — parses natural language price ranges, comfort attributes, and activity use cases in a single query. Instant semantic matching without separate NLP microservice.
findings.expected_behavior: Results filtered to ≤$100 items, ranked by comfort attributes
findings.prospect_description: Foot Locker's core 16-35 demographic commonly searches with price qualifiers. The /zgw gateway returns results but ignores price constraints — budget-conscious shoppers see $200 shoes when searching 'under 100'.

findings.title: Federated Search Absent: 'return policy' Returns No Content Pages
findings.impact_stat: Search-influenced digital revenue estimated at ~$480M-$800M/year based on 30-40% of $1.6-2.0B digital base
findings.actual_behavior: Page returned 102KB — identical file size to no-results page, confirming content pages are NOT indexed in product search
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Federated Search — index products, editorial content, brand pages, and policy documents in unified search. Single query surfaces all content types.
findings.expected_behavior: Return/exchange policy page as top result
findings.prospect_description: Foot Locker's custom /zgw gateway is products-only. Shoppers searching for return policies, sizing guides, or brand editorial content see zero results and abandon — or worse, call support.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Reduced irrelevant results, fewer returns; Meriel Neighbour, Global Head of Digital Product Delivery & Transformation at Clarks: 'Algolia allowed us to catapult ahead and start using AI in terms of a recommendation engine'

findings.title: Intent Detection Failure: 'Jordan' Not Detected as Brand
findings.impact_stat: Footwear ecommerce cart abandonment rate: 75.5-76.0% — intent detection failures directly amplify this
findings.actual_behavior: Page returned 100KB — small page consistent with generic/filtered results rather than a brand discovery experience
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia NeuralSearch + Rules Engine — brand-intent detection routes 'Jordan' queries to curated brand page or applies Jordan Brand boost rules automatically.
findings.expected_behavior: Jordan Brand page or results filtered/sorted by Jordan Brand
findings.prospect_description: Jordan Brand is Foot Locker's highest-margin product line. Shoppers searching 'Jordan' expect a curated brand experience — not generic mixed results. The /zgw gateway has no semantic brand-intent detection.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: AI Search + omnichannel across 3,400+ stores — same brand-intent problem solved at direct competitor scale

findings.title: No-Results Recovery: Bare Page with No Recommendations
findings.impact_stat: Shoe Carnival achieved up to 3.5x conversions from search with Algolia — Query Suggestions on no-results pages is a documented conversion lever
findings.actual_behavior: 102KB page — low-content, consistent with a minimal 'no results found' message without recovery UX
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Query Suggestions + Recommend — transforms no-results pages into discovery experiences with trending products and popular search terms.
findings.expected_behavior: Helpful recovery page — popular searches, product recommendations, category navigation
findings.prospect_description: Foot Locker's no-results page appears to be a dead end. No product recommendations, no popular searches, no category navigation. Shoppers who hit no-results exit instead of discovering alternatives.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: up to 3.5x conversions from search after deploying Algolia Search + Recommendations

findings.title: Dynamic Facets Absent: Basketball Shoes Show Generic Filters
findings.impact_stat: Dynamic faceting is a standard Algolia capability — reducing browse friction for activity-specific shoppers directly improves add-to-cart rates
findings.actual_behavior: 213KB results page — generic facets (brand, size, price) expected, no sport-specific contextual facets
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Dynamic Faceting — facets adapt to query context automatically. Basketball → ankle height, court surface. Running → stability type, terrain. Zero manual configuration per query.
findings.expected_behavior: Basketball-specific facets: ankle height, court type, position
findings.prospect_description: A shopper searching 'basketball shoes' has specific intent — ankle support type, court surface, guard vs forward position. Generic brand/size/price facets force manual scrolling through hundreds of results.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: AI-powered recommendations and faceting — reduced irrelevant results across 7,000+ SKUs

findings.title: Recommendations Engine: Zero Active Layer
findings.impact_stat: No vendor detected in BuiltWith scan — MyBuys and Monetate (historical) have been removed. Zero active recommendations layer.
findings.actual_behavior: 100KB 'sale' results page — no promotional banner detected. No recommendation vendor in live stack.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Recommend (Frequently Bought Together, Similar Items, Trending Items) — fills every surface where recommendations are absent with one integration.
findings.expected_behavior: Promotional banner + curated sale product merchandising + complementary product recommendations
findings.prospect_description: Foot Locker has no active recommendations engine. Every PDP visit, cart page, and no-results page is a missed upsell and cross-sell opportunity. The historical vendors (MyBuys, Monetate) were removed and not replaced.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Doubled merchandising productivity alongside up to 3.5x search conversion lift

findings.title: Search Intelligence: No Analytics Surface in Results
findings.impact_stat: Without search intelligence, FL cannot know which queries fail, which products get hidden, or where conversion drops in the search funnel
findings.actual_behavior: No analytics badges or signals in any of 15 screenshots across all tested queries
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Analytics + Insights — click analytics, conversion tracking, revenue analytics, no-results dashboard. Full search funnel visibility enabling data-driven merchandising.
findings.expected_behavior: Trending badges, bestseller indicators, popularity-ranked results
findings.prospect_description: Foot Locker's search results show no analytics signals — no 'trending,' no 'bestseller,' no popularity ranking. The /zgw gateway generates no analytics feedback loop. Merchandisers are flying blind.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Revenue analytics and omnichannel search intelligence across 3,400+ stores

findings.title: Typo Tolerance: Partial (Correction Prompt Unknown)
findings.actual_behavior: Results returned (218KB — PASS), but whether correction prompt is shown is unknown without visual review
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia typo tolerance is built-in — automatic 'Did you mean?' corrections, phonetic matching, and keyboard-proximity typo handling. No separate configuration required.
findings.expected_behavior: Results returned AND 'Did you mean: Nike Air Max?' correction prompt visible
findings.prospect_description: The /zgw gateway handles some typos (returns results for 'nikee air max') but the quality of the correction UX is unknown. Industry standard includes a visible 'Did you mean?' prompt that builds shopper confidence.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: up to 3.5x conversions — typo tolerance is part of Algolia's core NeuralSearch package

findings.title: Latency: Custom /zgw Gateway Routing Overhead
findings.actual_behavior: Full page navigation for search results — custom /zgw routing adds latency vs CDN-served search APIs
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia globally distributed API (50+ POPs) — median 20ms response time globally. Native instant-search with no /zgw routing overhead.
findings.expected_behavior: Sub-100ms result display with instant-search UX
findings.prospect_description: Foot Locker's search routes through a custom /zgw gateway — adding routing latency vs Algolia's globally distributed CDN network. No instant-search (as-you-type) UX was observed.

findings.title: Merchandising Consistency: Search vs Browse Alignment Unknown
findings.actual_behavior: Cannot confirm from screenshot evidence — custom /zgw gateway makes consistent ranking rules between search and browse less likely
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia unified ranking — single Rules Engine governs both search result ranking and category page ranking. Consistent merchandising experience across all entry points.
findings.expected_behavior: Same products in same ranking order via search and category browse
findings.prospect_description: Custom /zgw gateways typically apply different ranking logic for search queries vs category browse — resulting in the same product appearing in different positions depending on how a shopper navigated. This inconsistency erodes shopper trust.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Doubled merchandising productivity through unified search and category merchandising

We documented 15 screenshots across the full search experience. Worth a 15-minute conversation?

# Loom Video Script — Foot Locker Search Audit

**Total target:** 2 minutes / 120 seconds
**Target word count:** 200–280 words

---

## HOOK (0–10 sec)

"I spent 30 minutes on footlocker.com and found three things that surprised me — and one of them directly connects to what JD Sports just did in 2024."

---

## DEMO (10–90 sec)

**[Show screenshot: `deliverables/screenshots/01-homepage.png`]**

"This is footlocker.com's homepage. The search bar is front-and-center. But what's powering it isn't what you'd expect — there's no named search vendor in the stack. All searches route through a custom internal gateway called `/zgw`."

*[Transition: switch to NLP screenshot]*

**[Show screenshot: `deliverables/screenshots/13-nlp-sneakers-under-100.png`]**

"We typed 'comfortable sneakers under 100 dollars' — a completely natural query. Here's what came back: products priced at $140, $160, $200. The price qualifier 'under 100' was invisible to the gateway. This is the NLP gap. At Foot Locker's scale — roughly 9.5 million monthly visitors — 20 to 30 percent of search queries include a qualifier like this. That's hundreds of thousands of failing searches every month."

*[Transition: switch to competitor context]*

**[Show screenshot: `deliverables/screenshots/09-intent-jordan.png`]**

"And here's the Jordan brand intent test. Jordan is Foot Locker's highest-margin product line. When a shopper types 'Jordan,' a best-in-class search engine fires a brand intent redirect — not a generic results grid. This screenshot shows the current result. Meanwhile, JD Sports — Foot Locker's direct competitor — went live on Algolia AI Search in 2024 across 3,400 stores. JD Sports also owns Hibbett Sports and Finish Line, though whether those banners run on Algolia is unconfirmed."

---

## CTA (90–120 sec)

"Three gaps: NLP semantic failure, Jordan intent detection, no personalization layer. And Foot Locker is in the middle of a Dick's acquisition with new leadership and an open platform decision window. That's the right moment to make a move.

I put together a full audit with 15 documented screenshots and a business case model. Happy to walk you through it in 15 minutes. [Your name], [your title], Algolia."

---

- Pause 1 second between screenshots for transitions
